Spiced Nuts

Served at: Fourth Sunday of Advent

Serves 8Prep 10 minCook 20 min

Spiced nuts are a warm, aromatic treat traditionally enjoyed on the Fourth Sunday of Advent, symbolizing the anticipation and festive spirit leading up to Christmas. These nuts are coated with a blend of spices and sugar, making them a perfect snack to share with family and friends during holiday gatherings.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups (300 g) mixed nuts (such as almonds, pecans, walnuts)
  • 1/4 cup (50 g) granulated sugar
  • 1 tablespoon (15 ml) water
  • 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground cloves
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 300°F (150°C).
  2. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone baking mat.
  3. In a medium saucepan, combine sugar, water, cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves, and salt over medium heat.
  4. Stir constantly until the sugar dissolves and the mixture starts to bubble, about 3-4 minutes.
  5. Remove from heat and stir in the vanilla extract.
  6. Add the mixed nuts to the saucepan and stir quickly to coat all nuts evenly with the spiced syrup.
  7. Spread the coated nuts in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.
  8. Bake for 15-20 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until the nuts are toasted and the coating is dry and crisp.
  9. Remove from oven and allow to cool completely on the baking sheet; the nuts will harden as they cool.
  10. Once cooled, break apart any clusters and serve or store in an airtight container.

Tips

  • Use a mix of your favorite nuts for varied texture and flavor.
  • Watch the nuts closely while baking to prevent burning.
  • For extra flavor, add a pinch of cayenne pepper for a subtle heat.
